second_order: writing and judging April Fools patch notes
theme_note: These codes hold together because participants make the mock notes as a group and judge their effort or desirability; responses vary from praise and wanting changes implemented to calling the notes cringey.

second_order: recasting raid talk in SAB joke terms
theme_note: Participants carry the joke into raid advice by treating baubles and joke weapons as requirements; the turns vary between asking, steering a newcomer, and ranking players.

second_order: performing the Kormir-to-Colin subreddit makeover
theme_note: Participants inhabit and elaborate the room's visual joke through praise, mock complaint, flair, chants, and later Colin imagery; what varies is whether they celebrate, parody, or grumble while still addressing the makeover.

second_order: making the subreddit theme usable
theme_note: Participants negotiate how the seasonal stylesheet can be lived with by reporting readability problems, disabling it, repairing it, defending it, or supplying alternatives; the remedies and evaluations vary while the shared practice is practical theme work.

second_order: policing acceptance of the infantile-mode joke
theme_note: Participants establish the raid joke as familiar and tell critics how lightly to take it; they vary between finding it funny and rebuking resistance.

second_order: exploring qT's altered build pages
theme_note: Participants follow the changed build site, work around its cache, make its puns, and report what its icons do; the common practice is jointly inspecting the external joke.

second_order: playing and extending Super Charrio Kart
theme_note: Participants treat the playable joke as a game to try, review, troubleshoot, speedrun, improve, and build community around; contributions vary from technical reports and feature requests to mock career moves and later benchmark lore.

second_order: testing and exposing fake guides
theme_note: Participants act on straight-faced instructions, amplify their claimed success, then recognise or reveal the edit; reactions vary from praise for craft to anger at time wasted.

second_order: staging and answering the elite-new-player prank
theme_note: The mock request and its 'git gub' answer form one small call-and-answer performance.

second_order: renaming infantile mode as challenge mode
theme_note: This single proposal performs its own inversion and belongs with no other practice in the pool.

second_order: presenting and checking fake game developments
theme_note: Participants present plausible nerfs, releases, leaks, products, or news in an announcement register and test or correct their reality; the artifacts vary, as do playing along, verification, and correction.

second_order: arguing over the missing in-game April Fools tradition
theme_note: Participants compare patch notes with earlier in-game gags, explain why larger jokes stopped, and propose what should return; positions vary from regret and blame to accepting that doing nothing also provokes complaints.

second_order: recruiting and planning a Guild Wars canvas image
theme_note: Participants call for help, volunteer, request a shared plan, and circulate sources or instructions; later instances vary between Reddit recruitment, Discord proposals, and a separate Guild Wars 1 appeal.

second_order: placing, moving, and protecting the 898,526 logo
theme_note: Participants report pixels and progress, react to erasure or overwriting, move or shrink the drawing, script it, and protect its smile; the outcome varies across repeated losses and partial rebuilding.

second_order: wanting fake products to become real
theme_note: Participants fall for prank products and then judge the invented offerings more desirable than actual ones; reactions range from excitement and disappointment to saying the pranksters fooled themselves.

second_order: gaming search results with upvote campaigns
theme_note: Participants coordinate votes to make Guild Wars images lead searches, while others parody, defend, or reject the campaigns as karma seeking; the target phrases vary but the upvote tactic is shared.

second_order: negotiating room with neighboring drawings
theme_note: Participants respond to lost space by asking other groups for room, proposing peace, and reducing their own design at a border; the prospective requests and completed neighbour exchange vary in how far negotiation proceeds.

second_order: turning stray game oddities into April Fools jokes
theme_note: These small exchanges convert a talking wolf and a World 3 problem into collaborative joke premises; their objects differ, but participants answer an oddity by extending the gag.

second_order: asking for canvas representation as placement ends
theme_note: Late posts ask where a quaggan or game logo is, and the surviving answer says placement has ended; the requests share belated representation rather than visible organising.

second_order: recognising the Protect the smile reference after placement ended
theme_note: This single late code belongs with no other practice: it records retrospective recognition of the canvas slogan rather than recruitment, pixel work, or protection itself.
